recipes.name: Grilled Garlic and Herb Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning, or to taste
2 pounds large shrimp (21-25 per pound), peeled and deveined

steps.text: Whisk paprika, garlic, Italian seasoning, lemon juice, olive oil, pepper, basil, and brown sugar together in a bowl until thoroughly blended.
Stir in shrimp and toss to evenly coat with the marinade. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, turning once.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat. Lightly oil grill grate, and place about 4 inches from heat source.
Remove shrimp from marinade, drain excess, and discard marinade.
Place shrimp on preheated grill and cook, turning once, until opaque in the center, 5 to 6 minutes. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Garlic and Herb Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Delicious grilled shrimp flavored with a fresh lemon, garlic, paprika, and herb marinade are cooked on a hot grill until juicy, tender, and smoky.

video.description: You’ll love how a delicate marinade enhances the smoky flavor of these delicious grilled shrimp. Begin with a marinade of paprika, garlic, Italian seasoning, lemon juice, olive oil, pepper, basil and brown sugar. Toss 2 pounds of large shrimp in the sauce and marinate for a couple of hours. Remove from the sauce and put the shrimp on a hot grill and cook until done. It’s that simple! Convince eaters who are resistant to shrimp and blow away dedicated shrimp lovers. This delicious seafood will become a fast favorite and sure to become part of your regular summer grilling repertoire.

review.reviewBody: Excellent marinade! My husband isn't a huge fan of grilled shrimp, but we were having his Mom over and we both love the stuff so we got our turn on the grill. All I added to this marinade was a little dry white wine and I did cut the brown sugar way back to 1 tsp. because I really wanted the garlic and herb flavor to come through vs. a sweet flavor. But I still wanted to stick to the recipe. I skewered the shrimp onto bamboo skewers and marinated it for a couple hours. It turned out so good - I would definitely make this again!

I followed the recipe Exactly. I marinated them for 24 hours and slightly salted the skewers 15 minutes before they went on the Big Green Egg. Cooked them 3 minutes per side at 400 degrees and it was THE MOST DELICOUS SHRIMP EVER!!

Great flavor profile but of I can't help but tinker. Our house likes spice so I added a half teaspoonish each of cayenne, red pepper flakes, and salt. To taste of course. I mixed and tasted dry ingredients first. Once to taste, I added wet ingredients to a zip lock and let hang out for 3ish hours before adding shrimp to marinade for a couple hours. I used a lightly oiled cast iron skillet and got it medium high hot, cooked shrimp in batches. Maybe 2-3 minutes a side. Don't overload each batch or else they will steam and you won't get good caramelization. Be sure to scrape all juices and seasonings out between batches or else it will burn. The flavor combo was on point. We served 4 adults with varying levels of pallets and all couldn't keep their hands off. Devoured before anything else could be cooked.

I adjusted the recipe to be made stovetop and it worked out very well. I cooked the shrimp in a sautee pan with all of the marinade, then removed the shrimp, added a touch of corn starch to the marinade, and simmered it for a few minutes to thicken. Finally, I tossed the shrimp in the marinade/sauce and served it over lemon-garlic pasta. My husband and I both agreed that the shrimp were a touch sweet so next time I'll adjust for that.

Served as appetizer. Everyone loved it. Minor adjustments: Used very large shrimp (13/20), marinated 3 hrs., cut back on the brown sugar (1 tbls), doubled up on the garlic, used fresh basil and parsley, roasted at 425 for 5 minutes instead of saute. Two thumbs up!
Yes I made changes . I added a little salt and lime juice . Since I couldn’t use outdoors grill because of rain I added liquid smoke and I pan grilled . I loved the taste it had lots of flavor .

Made this according to the directions, substituting Old Bay for the Italian seasoning and holding off on the lemon juice until just before grilling as others have suggested. It was good, but not great. The Old Bay along with the black pepper made it a bit too spicy for us and seemed to be a bit overpowering. There was a definite sweetness to the flavor from the brown sugar. I think next time I'll drastically cut the Old Bay if I use it at all. Also, without the lemon juice in the marinade, it comes out like a heavy, thick paste. More liquid is needed in some form to make it a marinade you can work with - perhaps a bit of white wine or even plain water.

Very flavorful and so simple to make. I marinated it for 1 hour due to time constraints, used 1 TBSP brown sugar, fresh basil. Had it with fresh green salad. So delicious!!! Thank you berly15216 for this great, easy recipe. It will be a regular this summer!!

Herbed flavor for sure! I was only able to marinate mine for about 1/2 hour due to getting a late start on dinner preps, and yet the flavors stood out immensely. So easy to prepare. No time to heat up coals so I made indoors on a stovetop griddle. With those things in mind, this could be a quick weeknight dinner. I really appreciated that I had all ingredients in the house already. I just had to buy the shrimp and a vegetable and there was dinner! I did substitute 2 packets of Splenda for the brown sugar and you couldn't tell. With a vegetable side, we had a very low carb dinner (husband is diabetic). For those who like a bit of heat, sprinkle red pepper flakes on some of the skewers. I plan to make this addition in future executions.

Wow. This recipe is seriously amazing. I was initially worried about the amount of brown sugar. But against my instinct, I followed the recipe exactly and used the full 2 tbsp. It did not overpower the taste of anything. SO amazingly good. Someone else grilled on my pellet grill. We heated up to around 425 degrees, but were also grilling in the rain, so everytime we opened the hatch the temp dropped. In no rain, we will do 3 minutes on each side. In the rain, needed to add an extra 3 minutes at the end. Didn't realize until I was eating, but person manning the grill also included low smoke (pellet grill feature). Holy moly. As someone that likes shrimp, but it's kind of low on the preference scale, this recipe is amazing. Ate SO many shrimp that night. Definitely saving this recipe. Thank you!!

This was a giant hit at my Superbowl party! Only alteration was honey in the marinade versus brown sugar. 1 hr in the fridge, cooked on an indoor grilled. Lightly caramelized, herbaceous perfection that people could not stop raving about!
Very easy and delicious! Instead of putting them on skewers I used a grill pan. I just paired it with grilled corn on the cob. Will definitely make again.
First time grilling shrimp. Turned out great.

We used this marmalade on large scallops we had frozen in the freezer. It was perfect to cut the sweetness of the scallops and it was a recipe without butter! We both think butter makes the scallops too rich. We loved the combination of flavors. I did add some salt to increase the depth of the flavors. My husband said he wants this one in the rotation.
We have made these shrimp many many times and we absolutely love them. They are a regular in our recipe rotation.
